# Test fixtures

The real OpenEXR files are fetched by `node packages/environment/scripts/fetch-fixtures.mjs` from
AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr-images commit e38ffb0790f62f05a6f083a6fa4cac150b3b7452.
The fetcher pins SHA-256 4bf318bfdd9a8371694f8009be5d9ff21d4af8b73f444e34a5a047b8253c83e2
(BrightRings.exr) and eede573a0b59b79f21de15ee9d3b7649d58d8f2a8e7787ea34f192db3b3c84a4
(AllHalfValues.exr). Both match the existing fixture bytes. No OpenEXR implementation is fetched.

Fixtures are used only by the tests and are not part of the published package (`files` is `dist`).

- `synthetic-*.exr` and `synthetic-*.f32` were generated by `generate.py` with the reference OpenEXR library. `reference.json` holds digests of the real files decoded by that library (EXR) and of `sun_sky.hdr` (written by `scripts/make-hdr-fixture.js` from its own RGBE bytes; the independent Python RGBE decoder in `generate.py` recomputes the same entry).
- `BrightRings.exr` and `AllHalfValues.exr` come from the OpenEXR test images,
  https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr-images (`TestImages/`), under this license:

- `sun_sky.hdr` is Margo-made: `scripts/make-hdr-fixture.js` computes its RGBE pixels (sky gradient, sun disc, dither
  strip), writes the file and records its decoded digest in `reference.json`. It contains no third-party data.

- `piz/*.exr` are Margo-made PIZ files written by a scratch encoder from the PIZ format description, with
  `piz/roundtrip.json` (their expected decoded digests, computed from the source samples) and `piz/exr-piz.json`
  (digests and damaged-file outcomes for every EXR fixture here). They contain no third-party data.
